headline: Pretrained sequence models target DNA, RNA, and protein prediction tasks
label: Biological Sequence Foundation Models
summary: Recent preprints extend self-supervised DNA, RNA, and protein language models to alignment, glycosylation, epitope, and enzyme-function prediction.
synthesis: The dominant thread is pretrained sequence representations applied to downstream prediction, though the items span distinct modalities. IsoAlign pretrains DNA foundation models via isoform-aware DNA-protein alignment using two JEPA variants. LIMBER is a hybrid self-attention and Mamba RNA model pretrained on 40.5M ncRNA sequences. MaskNGly applies protein language model embeddings zero-shot to N-glycosylation site prediction, matching supervised predictors. PALM adapts ESM2 with LoRA and a BiLSTM for domain, functional-site, and zero-shot missense effect prediction. CARTnet adds contact-aware attention and template epitope information to B-cell epitope prediction. MIL-BC models proteins as bags of automatically detected domains for EC number prediction, improving F1 by 0.03-0.17. What is new is the integration of domain, contact, or template information with general sequence embeddings rather than sequence alone.
